facts.text: Standards bodies are organizations that run committees, hold votes and publish standards.
facts.quote: Standards bodies are the organizations that run the committees, hold the votes and publish the standards.

facts.text: The International Organization for Standardization (ISO) publishes international standards across almost all subjects, including earth-moving machinery standards central to heavy off-road machine validation.
facts.quote: The International Organization for Standardization (ISO) publishes international standards for almost everything, including the earth-moving machinery standards at the heart of the booklet.

facts.text: The International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) covers electrical and electronic matters and publishes IEC 61508 for functional safety and IEC 61496 for safety sensors.
facts.quote: The International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) covers electrical and electronic matters; IEC 61508 (functional safety) and IEC 61496 (safety sensors) are its work.

facts.text: Joint standards documents carry the participating bodies' names: ISO/IEC TR 5469 names ISO and IEC, while ISO/IEC/IEEE 15288 also names the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE).
facts.quote: Joint documents carry both names, as in ISO/IEC TR 5469, or three when the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE) takes part, as in ISO/IEC/IEEE 15288

facts.text: The European Committee for Standardization (CEN) and its electrical sister CENELEC publish EN standards; many adopt ISO texts, including EN ISO 16001:2017.
facts.quote: In Europe, the European Committee for Standardization (CEN) and its electrical sister CENELEC publish "EN" standards. Many adopt ISO texts (EN ISO 16001:2017)

facts.text: European-only standards include EN 474 for earth-moving machinery and the railway standards EN 14363 and EN 50716.
facts.quote: others are European only, such as EN 474 for earth-moving machinery and the railway standards EN 14363 and EN 50716

facts.text: The booklet lists CEN and CENELEC's joint artificial-intelligence committee JTC 21 as not verified.
facts.quote: Their joint artificial-intelligence committee, JTC 21, is listed by the booklet as not verified [Chapter 3].

facts.text: ASAM (Association for Standardization of Automation and Measuring Systems) publishes file formats that simulators use to exchange roads, scenarios, sensor data and materials.
facts.quote: ASAM (Association for Standardization of Automation and Measuring Systems) publishes the file formats simulators use to exchange roads, scenarios, sensor data and materials

facts.text: The booklet reports ASAM's own statement that no standardized metrics yet exist for judging simulation quality.
facts.quote: the booklet notes ASAM's own statement that no standardized metrics yet exist for judging simulation quality [Chapter 11].

facts.text: SAE International publishes SAE J1939, the network language used by ISO/TS 21815-2 to let a collision device request that a machine slow or stop.
facts.quote: SAE International publishes SAE J1939, the network language ISO/TS 21815-2 uses to let a collision device ask a machine to slow or stop [Chapter 3].

facts.text: Underwriters Laboratories (UL) publishes UL 4600 for autonomous products.
facts.quote: Underwriters Laboratories (UL) publishes UL 4600 for autonomous products [Chapter 12].

facts.text: Standards Australia publishes AS 21815.1:2023, a modified adoption of ISO 21815-1.
facts.quote: Standards Australia publishes AS 21815.1:2023, a modified adoption of ISO 21815-1 [Chapter 3].

facts.text: CSA Group, formerly the Canadian Standards Association, publishes CSA M424 for mining machines; the booklet did not verify CSA M424.
facts.quote: CSA Group (formerly the Canadian Standards Association) publishes CSA M424 for mining machines, not verified by the booklet [Chapter 3].

facts.text: The British Standards Institution (BSI) circulated the draft of ISO 21815-5 for comment in 2025.
facts.quote: The British Standards Institution (BSI) circulated the draft of ISO 21815-5 for comment in 2025 [Chapter 3].

facts.text: DIN, the German Institute for Standardization, performs the national standards-body role in Germany, but the booklet does not cite DIN directly.
facts.quote: DIN, the German Institute for Standardization, plays the same role in Germany; the booklet does not cite it directly.

facts.text: ISO and IEC texts provide an international baseline, whereas EN texts can carry legal weight in Europe.
facts.quote: an ISO or IEC text is an international baseline, an EN text can carry legal weight in Europe

facts.text: For assessing a standards document's reach in the machine-validation program, ASAM texts are engineering file formats, while a national adoption may differ from the original for a machine sold in that country.
facts.quote: an ASAM text is an engineering file format, and a national adoption may differ from the original for a machine sold in that country [Chapter 3].
